findings.title: `organization_context.member` can be None, so every audit-log GET can raise AttributeError
findings.body: `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` runs on every request, not only when `optimized_pagination=true`. `RpcUserOrganizationContext.member` is None when the caller is not an org member, for example an org auth token or API key. For any non-superuser caller in that situation, `None.has_global_access` raises AttributeError and the endpoint returns a 500, even on the default path. This regresses an endpoint that worked before. Compute it lazily and guard for None, for example `member and member.has_global_access`, only when `use_optimized` is set.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key cannot handle the datetime key the audit-log endpoint uses
findings.body: The endpoint pairs `OptimizedCursorPaginator` with `order_by="-datetime"`. `get_item_key` copies `Paginator`'s numeric logic and calls `math.floor`/`math.ceil` on `item.datetime`, which raises TypeError for a `datetime`. `DateTimePaginator` avoids this by converting to epoch milliseconds. `value_from_cursor` also returns the raw integer cursor value instead of converting it back to a datetime, so the `datetime >= <int>` filter built in `build_queryset` would be wrong. As a result the optimized path fails with a 500 whenever there are results, and it would paginate incorrectly even if it didn't crash.

findings.title: Negative-offset slicing is not supported by Django; comments claiming otherwise are wrong
findings.body: The comments say "The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically" and that negative offsets give "access to data beyond normal pagination bounds". Django querysets raise `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported` for `queryset[-n:m]`. Any client-supplied cursor with a negative offset, which `Cursor.from_string` accepts, produces a 500 on this path. The `cursors.py` comment, which says negative offsets are allowed for "efficient reverse pagination", is equally misleading, since nothing changes there. The `elif len(results) == offset + limit + extra` check further down also assumes the unclamped offset. Remove the negative-offset path, or implement it explicitly and validate it. The 'safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level' justification should not be relied on for user-controlled offsets.

findings.title: Unrelated behavior change in shared BasePaginator.get_result
findings.body: `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` changes the core paginator used by many endpoints. For forward cursors, a negative offset is now silently clamped to 0 instead of being rejected, so a malformed cursor returns the first page. For `is_prev` cursors the negative offset is still passed straight to the queryset, which fails exactly as before. The comment claims this enables 'efficient bidirectional pagination', but it does neither. It is unrelated to the spans-buffer change in this PR and has no tests.

findings.title: Redirect-following depth limit reduced 10x without justification
findings.body: The loop bound was changed from `0, 10000` to `0, 1000`, and the comment explaining the limit was deleted. The PR is about eviction and does not mention this. Segment trees with parent chains deeper than 1000 now stop following redirects early, so they can be split into multiple segments, a data-correctness regression for deep traces. Revert it, or document and test the new limit.

findings.title: Hard-coded 1000-span cap conflicts with `max_segment_spans` and evicts silently
findings.body: The script evicts down to a hard-coded 1000 members with `zpopmin`. `SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans` still defaults to 1001 and is no longer used anywhere, because the Python-side check in `_load_segment_data` was removed. The configured limit and the real limit now disagree and the parameter is dead. Previously an oversized segment logged an error and emitted `segment_span_count_exceeded`. Now spans are dropped silently, with no metric or log for how many were evicted. Pass the limit into the script as an ARGV value from `max_segment_spans`, and have the script or caller emit a metric when it evicts.

findings.title: ZUNIONSTORE defaults to SUM aggregation, which corrupts timestamp scores for duplicates
findings.body: Scores are now span end timestamps, and eviction relies on `zpopmin` removing the oldest. `zunionstore` defaults to `AGGREGATE SUM`. If the same payload is present in both sets being merged, for example after a Kafka redelivery, its score is added to itself and becomes roughly 2×timestamp. That span is then treated as the newest and survives eviction ahead of genuinely newer spans. Use `AGGREGATE MAX` (or `MIN`). The same applies to the second union on line 53.

findings.title: Switching segment keys from SET to ZSET under the same key names breaks rolling deploys
findings.body: The `span-buf:s:*` keys keep the same names but change type from SET (`sadd`/`scard`/`sunionstore`/`sscan`) to ZSET (`zadd`/`zcard`/`zunionstore`/`zscan`). Keys written by the old version live for up to `redis_ttl` (1h). During or after deployment, any existing set-typed key hit by `zadd`, `zcard`, `zunionstore` or `zscan` fails with WRONGTYPE. That fails the batch or the flush and crashes or loops the consumer. Old and new consumers running side by side will also conflict. Use a new key prefix, or flush or drain the buffer before rollout.

findings.title: No test covers the new eviction behavior
findings.body: The PR is titled 'eviction during insert', but the tests only add `end_timestamp_precise` to existing fixtures. Nothing exercises inserting more than 1000 spans into a segment, checking that the oldest-by-end-timestamp spans are the ones evicted, or checking that eviction works across merged sets and with root-span flags. There is also no test for the new ZSET scoring or the removed span-count check. Likewise, `OptimizedCursorPaginator` and the new `optimized_pagination` endpoint path have no tests, which is how the datetime and negative-offset failures went unnoticed.
